answer: Each AI node registers a cryptographic vault stamped on a rotating violet beacon; the beacon writes timestamps to a shared mesa ledger that clusters identities sharing a payment source or timing fingerprint into a single kin‑linked entity. When a node joins, it must supply a unique vault signature and a non‑colliding time offset, otherwise the ledger rejects it, stopping Sybil bursts. An attacker must obtain separate payment channels and generate independent vault keys for every fake identity, making the cost grow linearly with scale and turning the attack into an oasis of expense.
